meta.scopeNote: Reusable topology derived from historical planning. Resource names and sizing are illustrative, not deployed inventory. No selected account, deployment authorization, current quota/policy/cost approval, live RBAC, or end-to-end integration is asserted. Bicep is the deployment implementation; this JSON is a reference document.

inputs.userGoal: Provide a reusable read-only public-repository insight reference architecture; customer deployment requires separate authorization and validation.
subGoals: Zero-touch source boundary: public read-only access with no BC Gov repository changes
Target environment: Canada Central default, zone-redundant evidence storage, PostgreSQL, and reference web sizing; verify policy, residency, capacity, and cost before use
Explicit access mode: internal bootstrap, public fixture only, or authenticated pilot with trusted platform auth and approved tenant allowlist
Actual dashboard remains a 12-record synthetic-analysis fixture of target 100; collection-to-PostgreSQL-to-dashboard integration is not verified

reasoning.whyChosen: Provides a single lifecycle, policy, and cost-management boundary for the one production environment.
reasoning.tradeoffs: A single resource group intentionally matches the one-environment requirement; service-level identities and RBAC still isolate data access.

resources.name: id-gitinsights-web

reasoning.whyChosen: Limits the authenticated dashboard to read-only evidence and explicitly granted database permissions.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Adds identity resources and RBAC assignments in exchange for a smaller compromise blast radius.

resources.dependencyReasoning: The identity is created in the workload resource group.

reasoning.whyChosen: Isolates GitHub OAuth secret access and metadata evidence writes to the collector.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Requires separate RBAC assignments.

reasoning.whyChosen: Allows scan artifact access without granting Key Vault or Foundry permissions.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Requires separate RBAC assignments.

reasoning.whyChosen: Scopes Foundry inference and AI artifact writes to the synthesizer.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Requires separate RBAC assignments.

reasoning.whyChosen: Keeps PostgreSQL administration off every long-running application and job identity.
reasoning.tradeoffs: A post-provision bootstrap step must create least-privilege application roles.

reasoning.whyChosen: Centralizes Container Apps platform logs and Application Insights telemetry with bounded POC retention.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Usage-based ingestion adds cost, so source content is excluded and a daily cap is applied.

reasoning.whyChosen: Captures request, dependency, job, latency, and failure telemetry without making observability part of the functional path.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Sampling reduces cost but can omit individual traces; PostgreSQL business telemetry is a target integration, not current dashboard behavior.

resources.name: kv-gitinsights-poc

reasoning.whyChosen: Stores the unavoidable GitHub OAuth and Entra web application secrets with managed-identity access and recoverability controls.
reasoning.tradeoffs: The public endpoint remains enabled for the POC but requires Entra authentication and RBAC; private access is a production hardening step.

resources.dependencyReasoning: Only the web and collector identities can resolve their specific Key Vault-backed Container Apps secrets.

resources.name: stgitinsightspoc

reasoning.whyChosen: Preserves immutable and open-format evidence separately from the query database with zone-resilient production storage.
reasoning.tradeoffs: ZRS costs more than LRS but protects production evidence and control manifests from a zonal failure.

resources.dependencyReasoning: Container-scoped roles isolate raw/control ownership, scan artifacts, AI output, and read-only dashboard access.

references.title: Authorize access to blobs with Microsoft Entra ID

resources.name: psql-gitinsights-poc

reasoning.whyChosen: Supports interactive filtering, graph relationships, lineage, transactions, and future curation with an open relational engine.
reasoning.tradeoffs: General Purpose zone-redundant compute and geo-redundant backup increase cost but remove the POC database's largest availability risk.

resources.dependencyReasoning: A dedicated bootstrap identity is the Entra administrator; application roles are created separately with least privilege.

references.title: Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server

resources.name: aif-gitinsights-poc

reasoning.whyChosen: Provides governed model inference, projects, Entra authentication, evaluation, tracing, and model flexibility for evidence-cited synthesis.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Introduces an Azure AI dependency and variable inference cost; the deterministic product remains functional without it.

resources.dependencyReasoning: Only the synthesis identity receives a Foundry data-plane role; traces flow to Application Insights.

resources.name: proj-gitinsights-poc

reasoning.whyChosen: Scopes the model endpoint, evaluation artifacts, traces, and identity used by the synthesis workload.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Adds a managed project resource but avoids deploying an autonomous agent for the batch path.

resources.dependencyReasoning: The project is a child of the Foundry account.

resources.name: model-gitinsights-poc

reasoning.whyChosen: Keeps model choice and capacity explicit and deploys only after quota is confirmed.
reasoning.tradeoffs: The infrastructure cannot be fully provisioned until a supported model/version and quota are selected.

resources.dependencyReasoning: The deployment belongs to the Foundry account and is consumed through its project endpoint.

resources.name: cae-gitinsights-poc

reasoning.whyChosen: Hosts the SSR application and bounded jobs with managed scaling and no Kubernetes operations.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Reference consumption sizing requires a current estimate and availability check. Private networking is not established by this plan; review the selected environment's current networking capabilities.

resources.dependencyReasoning: The environment sends platform and console logs to the workspace.

resources.name: ca-gitinsights-web

properties.externalIngress: configureEntraAuth OR publicDashboard; false for internal bootstrap

reasoning.whyChosen: Target SSR dashboard and server-side read-only API with mode-dependent access and one reference warm replica; current routes remain fixture-backed.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Keeping one warm replica increases baseline cost and reduces scale-from-zero delays; no availability or latency SLA is implied.

resources.dependencyReasoning: The app uses its dedicated identity, authenticated secrets, read-only evidence access, least-privilege database role, and telemetry.

reasoning.whyChosen: Refreshes the cohort and mutable GitHub metadata without a continuously running worker.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Polling is not real-time but preserves the zero-touch source boundary.

resources.name: caj-gitinsights-dbbootstrap
resources.subtype: Manual database migration and role bootstrap

reasoning.whyChosen: Runs migrations under the isolated database administrator identity and creates a read-only Entra role for the web identity.
alternativesConsidered: Make the web identity PostgreSQL administrator
Run privileged SQL from GitHub Actions
reasoning.tradeoffs: Adds a manual post-provision step but removes database administration from long-running workloads.

resources.dependencyReasoning: The job uses the dedicated administrator identity and grants the web identity only read permissions after migrations.

references.title: Manage Microsoft Entra roles in Azure Database for PostgreSQL

reasoning.whyChosen: Provides bounded ephemeral compute for cloning and deterministic scanning of only changed repositories.
reasoning.tradeoffs: A single job limits parallelism but simplifies rate, disk, and failure control for the first 100 repositories.

reasoning.whyChosen: Intended to process completed evidence bundles; the independent weekly schedule is not a scanner completion dependency.
alternativesConsidered: AI calls in the web request path
reasoning.tradeoffs: Independent schedules can lag or fail; operators must inspect scan errors and evidence lineage. Freshness acceptance criteria require customer agreement.

overallReasoning.summary: Target single-region topology with evidence storage, relational read models, workload-specific managed identities, observability, and optional advisory synthesis. Current dashboard behavior is fixture-backed, not a verified integrated deployment. GitHub remains a read-only source.
overallReasoning.tradeoffs: Reference sizing and public service endpoints require customer-specific cost, security, residency, policy, quota, and availability review. Public fixture access and authenticated pilot access are separate explicit modes; no private network or production SLA is supplied.

plan.validation: Reference dependencies are preserved for review, not certified as a current deployment. Recheck dependency topology, Bicep compilation, effective policies, resource inventory, regional SKU/model capacity, image provenance, parameter-matched what-if, and live RBAC after explicit account-owner authorization. Historical approvals and validation are not transferable.

Verify current inventory, policy, quota, PostgreSQL capacity, and optional Foundry model processing geography and capacity
Resolve or compensate for validation workflow omission of publicDashboard before relying on a public-mode what-if
Review immutable image digests, protected OIDC environment, parameter-matched what-if, secret bindings, and least-privilege role scope
Verify live endpoints, platform auth, tenant denial paths where applicable, managed identities, telemetry redaction, and actual read-model integration
Inspect manual job completion and partial failures before schedules; independent schedules are not orchestration
Record rollback, retention, final cost review, and authorized teardown verification

Single production environment with resilient state
